transitions.historical_text: Activate only by paying 1000 Life Points when a monster you control is destroyed and sent to the Graveyard, Special Summon 1 Level 4 monster from your Deck.
transitions.modern_text: When a monster you control is destroyed and sent to the Graveyard (except during the Damage Step): Pay 1000 Life Points; Special Summon 1 Level 4 monster from your Deck.
transitions.summary: Wording only, on Konami's period rulebook (round 035). v1 (LCYW-EN102) added "(except during the Damage Step)". Under Konami's rulebook (Versions 7.0 to 8.0) a Normal Trap Card could not be activated in the Damage Step in any case ("During the Damage Step, you can only activate Counter Trap Cards, or cards with effects that directly change a monster's ATK or DEF"), so the era card could not respond to a monster destroyed in battle, as the added words state. No TCG ruling read gives Soul Rope a Damage Step exception. The 2015 change (c1, "by a card effect") is untouched.

transitions.summary: Wording only, on period rulings (round 037, 2026-09-29). The record claimed: Era: triggers on any destruction of a monster you control that sends it to the Graveyard, including destruction by battle; modern: only destruction by a card effect, so battle destruction no longer triggers it. Era: any destruction that is neither battle nor a card effect (e.g. destruction as a cost) would also trigger it; modern: only destruction by a card effect. This is the 'unreproduced residual' named in the record's gap. A period ruling in force says otherwise: Konami's Official Rulebook Version 7.0: "During the Damage Step, you can only activate Counter Trap Cards, or cards with effects that directly change a monster's ATK or DEF. Also, these cards can only be activated up until the start of damage calculation." Konami's Official Rulebook Version 7.0: "A card is destroyed when it is sent to the Graveyard due to battle between monsters or by an effect that destroys a card. A card that is returned from the field to the hand or Deck, or, that is sent to the Graveyard as a cost or Tribute, is NOT considered "destroyed."" No difference between the era card and the modern card is established.

implementation_metadata.reason: Round 037 (2026-09-29): no generated card exists or is needed for this record. A period ruling in force says the era card played as the modern card does on every point the record claimed, so the modern implementation is used at the snapshots this record applies at.

review.notes:
upstream_implementations lists only 511001593 'Soul Rope (Anime)', a distinct card whose text ('When a monster(s) you control is destroyed: Pay 1000 LP; ...') matches no lineage version (ratio 0.7388) and which drops the 'sent to the Graveyard' requirement entirely; it is not substitutable, so the gap stands. It is a useful reference for the shape an era script needs: EVENT_DESTROYED with EFFECT_FLAG_DAMAGE_STEP and a cfilter carrying no REASON_EFFECT/REASON_DESTROY test, plus the 'sent to the Graveyard' requirement the anime card lacks. Dating: v0's earliest tcg date is tcg-oce 2008-01-01 at YEAR precision, with the NA/EU Special Edition at 2008-06-18; either way v0 is the text in force at both the GOAT and Edison snapshots, since v1 is 2012-09-29. No supported period snapshot falls inside the intermediate window 2012-09-29 .. 2015-11-12, so I attached no resulting_implementation to the first change - the intermediate version is not needed by any format. CAVEAT on that first change: the packet establishes that the '(except during the Damage Step)' exclusion was added, not that era policy independently permitted Damage Step activation of a trap whose trigger is general destruction rather than battle destruction specifically. I recorded the text fact and the inference, and flagged nothing further, because the era version is v0 under either reading and the gap is required by the second change regardless.

Round 035 (2026-09-29) correction. The Damage Step half of the round 031 script was contradicted by Konami's rulebook, Versions 7.0 (capture 2008-12-30), 7.1 (2010-03-30), 7.2 (2011-05-16) and 8.0 (linked from Konami's Gameplay page on 2011-09-18): only Counter Trap Cards and cards that directly change ATK or DEF may be activated in the Damage Step. The caveat above (this record inferred a Damage Step permission from the text alone) is resolved against it. Superseded summary of the first change, kept verbatim: "Activation window narrowed: v1 (LCYW-EN102) added '(except during the Damage Step)', which the v0 text (LODT-ENSE2) does not carry. v0 triggers whenever a monster you control is destroyed and sent to the Graveyard, and battle destruction happens inside the Damage Step, so under the era text the trap had to be usable there for its battle-destruction case to function at all. The same printing moved the 1000 Life Point payment from 'Activate only by paying 1000 Life Points when ...' into PSCT cost position, which does not change that it is a cost." Superseded implementation note, kept verbatim: "Round 031: implemented by a project-authored script under the custom-script strategy (data/custom-cards/c600000009.json; passcode 600000009). Previously recorded as a known gap with gap_reason "Project Ignis ships no historical implementation of this card; reproducing the era behaviour needs a custom script and a reserved passcode" (gap_sources ignis-babelcdb, yugipedia-card-errata). Status is partial, not complete: the custom card's not_reproduced list names what the script does not establish." Superseded gap statement, kept verbatim: "In a period format Soul Rope cannot be used when your monster is destroyed in battle - the era text's main case - because the modern card only triggers on destruction by a card effect and is barred from the Damage Step." Effect: the first change is cosmetic, the generated card 600000009 was removed and its number retired, and the state that applies at Edison and Tengu (before the 2015 change) is again a known gap for the remaining difference: the era card triggered on any destruction of a monster you control outside the Damage Step, the modern card only on destruction by a card effect. No scenario this repository can observe separates the two (destruction by battle is inside the Damage Step, where neither card may be activated); destruction that is neither a card effect nor battle is the residual case. Evidence: docs/research/period-rulings-generated-scripts.md, sections 4 and 6.8.

Round 037 (2026-09-29). Checked against period rulings: the differences the functional transition claims were searched for in the Konami-hosted UDE card FAQ (2008-12), the 2005 UDE card rulings page, Konami's errata lists, rulebooks and per-set ruling documents, and the archived UDE judge-list threads Yugipedia points to (the transition's rulings_check; docs/research/text-only-errata-audit.md, Soul Rope). A period ruling in force contradicts every difference the transition claimed: Era: triggers on any destruction of a monster you control that sends it to the Graveyard, including destruction by battle; modern: only destruction by a card effect, so battle destruction no longer triggers it. Contradicted by Konami's Official Rulebook Version 7.0: "During the Damage Step, you can only activate Counter Trap Cards, or cards with effects that directly change a monster's ATK or DEF. Also, these cards can only be activated up until the start of damage calculation." Konami's Official Rulebook Version 7.2: "During the Damage Step, you can only activate Counter Trap Cards, or cards with effects that directly change a monster's ATK or DEF. Also, these cards can only be activated up until the start of damage calculation." Era: any destruction that is neither battle nor a card effect (e.g. destruction as a cost) would also trigger it; modern: only destruction by a card effect. This is the 'unreproduced residual' named in the record's gap. Contradicted by Konami's Official Rulebook Version 7.0: "A card is destroyed when it is sent to the Graveyard due to battle between monsters or by an effect that destroys a card. A card that is returned from the field to the hand or Deck, or, that is sent to the Graveyard as a cost or Tribute, is NOT considered "destroyed."" Konami's Official Rulebook Version 7.2: "A card is destroyed when it is sent to the Graveyard due to battle between monsters or by an effect that destroys a card. A card that is returned from the field to the hand or Deck, or, that is sent to the Graveyard as a cost or Tribute, is NOT considered "destroyed."" The transition is cosmetic: no difference between the era card and the modern card is established. Verdicts: [c1] d1 contradicted at Edison, contradicted at Tengu; d2 contradicted at Edison, contradicted at Tengu. Superseded summary, kept verbatim: "Functional erratum: 'When a monster you control is destroyed and sent to the Graveyard' becomes 'When a monster you control is destroyed by a card effect and sent to the Graveyard', so the modern card no longer triggers on battle destruction at all. The modern script encodes the restriction in its cfilter, which requires both c:IsReason(REASON_EFFECT) and c:IsReason(REASON_DESTROY) on an EVENT_TO_GRAVE trigger." Superseded coverage, kept verbatim: kind: "known-gap"; gap_reason: "Round 035: the round 031 script was removed because it let the Trap be activated in the Damage Step, which Konami's period rulebook forbids. The remaining difference, that the era card triggered on any destruction of a monster you control outside the Damage Step while the modern card requires destruction by a card effect, is not reproduced and no engine test observes it."; gap_sources: ["konami-official-rulebook-v71-2010"; "yugipedia-card-errata"]. Superseded gap statement, kept verbatim: "In a period format EDOPro's Soul Rope triggers only on destruction by a card effect. The era card (before 2015-11-12) triggered on any destruction of a monster you control outside the Damage Step; ordinary play does not separate the two, because destruction by battle is inside the Damage Step, where neither card may be activated. Destruction that is neither a card effect nor battle is the unreproduced residual."
